# archestra_mcp_server (Data Source)

Finds an installed MCP server that exists already. Set at least one of `name`, `catalog_id`, `catalog_name` and `owner_email`; every one that is set must match, and exactly one installation must remain. Use `id` as the `mcp_server_id` of a tool assignment. People's own installations of one registry entry share a name, so select one with `owner_email`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# One person's connected Slack account: an installation made in the app.
# People's own installations of one registry entry share a name, so the owner
# selects it.
data "archestra_mcp_server" "slack" {
  catalog_name = "Slack"
  owner_email  = "release-manager@example.com"
}

data "archestra_tool" "slack_send_message" {
  name = "slack__slack_send_message"
}

# Give an agent that one tool, always run through that installation.
resource "archestra_agent" "announcer" {
  name          = "Release announcer"
  system_prompt = "Post a short note about each release."

  tools = [{
    tool_id                    = data.archestra_tool.slack_send_message.id
    mcp_server_id              = data.archestra_mcp_server.slack.id
    credential_resolution_mode = "static"
  }]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `catalog_id` (String) ID of the MCP registry entry the server was installed from.
- `catalog_name` (String) Exact name of the MCP registry entry the server was installed from.
- `name` (String) Exact name of the installation.
- `owner_email` (String) Email address of the person who owns the installation.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) ID of the installation.
- `scope` (String) Who the installation is shared with.
- `team_id` (String) Team the installation belongs to, for a team installation.
